description:
In repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/feature-compose.ts there is a landed but INERT block that tries to record a failure outcome against the compose lessons that preceded a failure. It never works: it calls a non-existent endpoint path, sends a wrong auth header, sends a wrongly-shaped body, and mis-types the response — and because it is fire-and-forget, all four fail in silence. Repair it in place by delegating to the resolver that already implements this correctly.

Anchor A — this line occurs exactly once and is inside the broken block:

                await fetch(`${CONCEPT_DB_ENDPOINT}/usage/${concept.id}/fail`, {

Anchor B — this line occurs exactly once, a few lines above it:

            interface ConceptRow { id?: string; }

Replace the broken block so that it does exactly two things.

FIRST, look up the lesson concept ids using the SAME call this file already makes when it recalls lessons — these literals are correct and must be copied exactly, not reconstructed:

  - URL:     `${DISCOVERY_ENDPOINT}/resolve`
  - method:  POST
  - headers: Content-Type application/json, plus an Authorization header whose value is `ApiKey ${apiKey}` built from process.env["METABOB_API_KEY"], set only when that env var is present
  - body:    JSON.stringify({ pointer: { type: "conceptSearch", source_type: "compose_lesson", query: cls, limit: 8 } })

  The response body is shaped { content?: Array<{ content?: string; id?: string }> } — note it is an OBJECT with a content array, NOT a bare array. Read the id off each row in that content array and keep the ones that are present.

SECOND, credit those ids by calling the existing resolver IN-PROCESS rather than re-implementing its HTTP:

  await resolveCreditPrimedConcepts({ type: "credit_primed_concepts", conceptIds: ids, outcome: "failure" });

For that call to compile you must also add this import alongside the other sibling-resolver imports near the top of the file:

  import { resolveCreditPrimedConcepts } from "./credit-primed-concepts.js";

Keep the whole thing best-effort: it must remain wrapped so any error or timeout is swallowed and can never fail or delay the compose. Do not add module-level variables. Do not change composeLessonsBlock. Do not change any other line in the file.

Verified by hand before dispatch: invoking credit_primed_concepts with conceptIds and outcome "failure" moved times_failed from 0 to 1 on a real concept, returning {"credited":1,"errors":0}. That call is known-good; the HTTP the current block performs is known-bad.
